title: Recipe 23 — PII Redaction and Encryption (three layers over the audit log)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Three layers, in order: redact before write, encrypt at rest, then delete on schedule. Each one is its own package and its own smoke.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed starter and the recipe are never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env into this one terminal.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the audit log the layers wrap

beats.label: Type recipe 11's managed harness
beats.cue: “All three layers sit on the multitenant audit log — so start from that starter, unchanged. Tenant isolation is the substrate, not a feature we add.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean first, so every finding after this belongs to a layer and not to the spec.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Two tenants, lowered. Redaction and encryption are runtime wiring around this — not new spec surface.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target managed

beats.label: Compile the bundle
beats.cue: “The redactor and the encryption wiring are in the emitted bundle — you can read them. The managed daemon is scaffolding; recipe 11 is where its boot gets proved.”

verify.note: emits the daemon bundle. Deliberately not --check: a managed daemon binds :3000, and --check scrubs the environment (so PORT cannot be overridden), which means exactly one driver in the suite may boot one — that is recipe 11's.

beats.label: Blank the policy file
beats.cue: “Layer 1 is per-tenant policy: which detectors run, and which PII a tenant is legitimately allowed to keep.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's per-tenant policy
beats.cue: “Tenant A redacts cards and SSNs and keeps email in plaintext; tenant B hashes everything under its own secret.”

beats.label: Read the two policies back
beats.cue: “Same file, parsed — one allow-list, one hash mode. Stricter overrides are the normal direction; the runtime permits either.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const p = Bun.YAML.parse(await Bun.file("live/pii-policy.yaml").text()); for (const t of p.tenants) console.log(t.id, "→", JSON.stringify(t.piiPolicy))'

beats.label: Run the redactor smoke
beats.cue: “Five built-in detectors plus the classifier slot, against a hundred PII samples: leakage zero percent. That is the layer's actual claim, measured.”

verify.note: ALL PROBES PASSED — ssn/credit-card/phone/email/iban detectors, replace + hash modes, leakage 0.0% < 5%

beats.label: Blank the record file
beats.cue: “Layer 2 changes what a line on disk looks like. This is the whole on-disk shape.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's encrypted record
beats.cue: “No plaintext anywhere: a nonce, a GCM tag, the KEK-wrapped data key, the KEK version, and the ciphertext.”

beats.label: Read the five fields back
beats.cue: “kekVersion is the whole trick — the reader picks the matching key, so a rotation never rewrites a line that is already on disk.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const r = await Bun.file("live/encrypted-record.json").json(); console.log("encrypted record fields:", Object.keys(r).join(", "), "· kekVersion", r.kekVersion)'

verify.note: encrypted record fields: iv, tag, wrappedDek, kekVersion, encryptedPayload · kekVersion 3

beats.label: Run the encryption smoke
beats.cue: “KEK to DEK wrapping, a round trip, then a rotation: new records carry the new kekVersion and old records still decrypt.”

verify.note: ALL PROBES PASSED — wrap/unwrap, bad-tag detection, rotation re-wraps without rewriting log lines

beats.label: Try the recipe's rotate command
beats.cue: “Exit 1, and the reason is the honest one: an env-var backend will not invent key material. Wire the file backend from recipe 20 and this is where onRotation fires.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — exit 1: 'secret "CREWHAUS_AUDIT_KEK" cannot be rotated via env-var backend without a newValue'. No secrets backend is configured in a scratch driver dir, so the deployment falls back to env vars; the recipe's rotation flow needs the file backend (recipe 20) or --value.

groups.title: One more thing · Layer 3 — retention windows

beats.label: Run the retention smoke
beats.cue: “Longer-duration-wins, active audit windows refusing a delete, and an idempotent sweep. Right-to-delete and right-to-export, end to end.”

verify.note: ALL PROBES PASSED — retain/shorten, audit-window override, purge, export, idempotent sweep

beats.label: Create the audit store
beats.cue: “The store is a directory the daemon creates on its first write. Nothing has served a request in this scratch harness, so make it by hand — the layer is about what happens once it exists.”

verify.note: without an existing .crewhaus/audit the retention commands below are honest no-ops ("no .crewhaus/audit store present, no evidence appended")

beats.label: Enforce retention on this harness
beats.cue: “A real sweep, not a dry run — and it appends its own audit record. The enforcement is itself evidence.”

beats.label: Export everything one tenant has
beats.cue: “Right-to-export: sessions plus audit day files plus the chain-tail anchor, so the export re-verifies standalone.”

verify.note: manifest.json written; complete audit export — _chain-tail.json included

beats.label: Dry-run right-to-delete
beats.cue: “And the guard: purge would delete expired records, but it keeps every audit day file, because removing one breaks verification of everything after it.”

verify.note: kept 1 audit day file(s) — audit chain integrity; dry run: nothing deleted, no evidence appended
